At 1k objects + 500 tombstones with 10 peers, the estimate is ~20-40 ms per frame at ~2 frames/s, a few % of the main thread. That is jank and very heavy flash and battery waste, not an ANR. Saturation is only plausible near design maximums (30-64 peers with 5-10k records).

There is no data loss, crash or non-convergence, so this is major waste: high, not critical.

Root cause confirmed. For every snapshot tombstone, validateRecordV3 calls findLocalIdForWireId (Android SyncManager.kt:2557-2566 → 2961-2977; iOS SyncManager.swift:3924-3931 → 4173-4196). A miss recomputes HMAC wireObjectId over lastContent, all waypoints and all drawings. On Android each call also does Mac.getInstance plus init (SyncIdentity.kt:55-61). Nothing short-circuits exact persisted tombstones before validation (the snapshot loop is at 1911-1932), and lastContent survives a v3 reconnect (the connect v3 branch 1062-1074 does not clear it; only detachMissionStateForKeyLock (451) and leave/dispose do). A whole snapshot page is validated inside one main-thread callback, and SyncInboundCallbackGate fails the socket after 10 s (SyncWebSocketTransport.kt:44-58, 132, 253-259, 323-329). The backoff resets only after the handshake (SyncReconnectBackoff.kt:12-13; SyncManager.kt:1857), so a device over the limit retries at up to 30 s forever, pulling a full snapshot each time.

Severity trimmed from critical to high. The claim of '~1,700 tombstones in one 900 KB page' only holds for tombstone-dominated pages. Records are keyed by random HMAC ids, so live puts (~1.3 KB) and tombstones (~0.5 KB) interleave. For example, 2k live + 1.7k tombstones gives ~4 pages of ~425 tombstones each: ~1.7M HMACs per page. That exceeds 10 s only at ≳5 µs per HMAC on ART, which was not measured on a device.
- The permanent non-convergence therefore needs multi-thousand-object rooms with thousands of historic deletes. That is plausible after importing and deleting large KMLs, but it is at the upper end of design capacity.
- Below that threshold, the result is multi-second main-thread freezes (Android ANR risk; iOS freezes, with no gate) on every reconnect.

The O(T×N) lookup is clearly a bug; the fix (build a wireId→localId map once) is cheap.

Confirmed on both clients.

Android, snapshot-end: after commitRemoteSnapshot inserts every pending marker (SyncManager.kt:1950), resolvePendingModelApplication runs for every record inside the same main-thread frame callback (1960-1966). For APPLY_INCOMING (2657-2667), each record does:
- upsertWaypoint → a linear any{} (2992-2996) → WaypointStore.add → commit/persistCandidate, a full-list sealed write (WaypointStore.kt:73-78, 258-266);
- a reexport linear scan (3005-3020);
- clearPendingModelApplication → a full replay save (SyncReplayState.kt:429-433).

The replay document starts larger than the auditor assumed, because every pending entry (~400 B) is present after commitRemoteSnapshot. At N=2,000 that is ~1.2 MB shrinking to ~0.2 MB, so on the order of GB of seal+fsync writes plus ~2,000 fsyncs, all in one callback. That exceeds both the 5 s ANR input timeout and the 10 s reader gate, so the socket is killed and a second snapshot follows. The second pass mostly takes the NONE/exact path, so it does converge eventually.

Outbound: syncLocalStateV3 does one reserveLocalPut (a full save) per object (1304-1336). It also hashes and HMACs every object before the lastContent check (1310-1316).

iOS: observeModelRevisions (SyncManager.swift:2013-2056) is an undebounced CombineLatest3 sink. It computes modelHashes, i.e. a GeoJSON export plus SHA-256 of every object (2058-2071), before it checks resolvingPendingModel. That is O(N²) during snapshot apply, and a full re-hash on every local edit. Joining a room with a few hundred to a few thousand objects is normal use, so high is right.

Confirmed. sendSnapshot builds `[...chunk, record]` and JSON.stringify()s the whole candidate page for every record (index.ts:1512-1519), inside blockConcurrencyWhile (index.ts:688).

Within a page this is quadratic. Overall it is O(N × page size): each record costs roughly half a 900 KB page of stringify, whatever the record size.

My independent vitest run in scratchpad/verify-S5-efficiency/test/v5.test.ts ('V5-04'):
- 10k records × 1 KB ct → 915 ms until the 101.
- Three concurrent connects to the same room took 2,810 ms. They are serialised, so all other room events wait.

Correction: 'approaches the 30 s blockConcurrencyWhile limit' is wrong. The 30 s limit applies per call, and each call is ~1 s at 10k records. The real risk is aggregate stall under a reconnect herd (e.g. 64 × ~0.9 s after a deploy or eviction) while clients' 20 s / 30 s handshake timers run.

This is significant wasted DO CPU on every connect (~27× the linear chunker) plus room-wide stalls at large sizes, so high stands.

Confirmed. processWebSocketMessage awaits touchActivity() after every handled type, including loc, chat and chat-key (index.ts:792-805). touchActivity is storage.put('meta:lastActivity') plus getAlarm (1564-1568); fetch also calls it after each snapshot (689).

My vitest 'V5-05a':
- 30 valid + 5 INVALID (replayed-counter) loc frames produced 35 puts, all to meta:lastActivity.
- handlePresenceV3's early returns (1415-1424) do not skip the write.

'V5-05b', with storage.put made to throw:
- The peer still received the loc broadcast.
- The sender was closed with 1011 'storage unavailable' (806-809).
- A new connect returned 503 (690-693).

Cloudflare's pricing docs (checked) confirm the limits for SQLite-backed DOs:
- KV put() is billed as rows written.
- Workers Free allows 100,000 rows written per day.
- 'further operations of that type will fail with an error' until 00:00 UTC.

wrangler.jsonc:18-19 explicitly advertises the Free plan for self-hosters. A 10-12 member unit sharing at 5 s exhausts the quota in ~12-14 h, and larger rooms much sooner. Every room on the account then fails closed until UTC midnight: a relay DoS in plausible use.

Any room member can also burn the quota at 200 frames/10 s (even invalid loc frames) ≈ 1.7M rows/day.

On Paid this is pure cost waste (medium there), but the Free-plan outage justifies critical.

Confirmed. sendSnapshot always lists every obj: row (index.ts:1507-1523). The client persists lastSnapshotSeq (SyncReplayState.kt:55, 177) but connect sends only the Authorization, X-Protocol and X-Room-Id headers (SyncManager.kt:1083-1090).

Reconnects happen on:
- every flap (handleSocketEnded 987-1031);
- iOS foreground return (updateLifecycle SyncManager.swift:992-993 → reconnectForForegroundReconciliation 1833-1853);
- Android unlock (prepareForForegroundUnlock/attachForegroundStores 468-501).

Every reconnect re-downloads and fully re-verifies every record (AES-GCM, Ed25519, GeoJSON parse/export, HMAC), with no skip for records that are byte-identical to already persisted state.

This is a design gap rather than a correctness bug, but the waste scales with room size: ~13 MB per reconnect at 10k records. There is also a relay-cost dimension the auditor did not quantify. Each connect reads N rows, so on Workers Free (5M rows read/day) a 10k-record room exhausts the read quota after ~500 connects/day (e.g. 20 members × 25 foreground returns). Snapshot reads would then fail → 503.

Suggested fix (a), a local skip of re-verification, is wire-compatible and cheap. High is reasonable given the stated bandwidth and relay-cost goals.

Confirmed.

Android: enterBackgroundPresenceOnly keeps the v3 socket (SyncManager.kt:387-417). handleMessage runs inspectText and charges liveReceiveBudget BEFORE the background drop (1773-1798).

iOS: the receive loop admits to the budget first, then discards when !foregroundReady (SyncManager.swift:1703-1726).

Keepalive stays at 20 s on both platforms: Java-WebSocket connectionLostTimeout=20 pings each interval regardless of traffic (SyncWebSocketTransport.kt:133, 285); iOS heartbeatInterval 20 (SyncManager.swift:657, 1885-1896).

The relay has no per-socket opt-out (broadcast index.ts:1556-1562). A burst over 200 frames/10 s closes the background socket (1008). On Android that path goes handleSocketEnded → backgroundTransportEnded (1029-1031) → UnitSyncRuntime.onBackgroundTransportEnded → invalidateAndStopService (UnitSyncRuntime.kt:254-257), so background sharing silently stops until unlock. The same happens on any network flap while locked.

Caveat on the scenario: if the whole patrol is screen-off at 15 min, inbound traffic is tiny. The ~39 MB/4 h figure assumes other members are foreground-sharing at 5 s. The waste is real in mixed rooms, and the 20 s ping alone is a meaningful radio-wake cost. High is fair.

Confirmed.

Client side: syncLocalStateV3 sends every changed object back to back, with no pacing or in-flight window (Android SyncManager.kt:1304-1336 → queueDelivery 1157-1163; iOS 2271-2314 → 2213-2219).

Relay side: it closes at 200 msgs or 4 MiB per 10 s (index.ts:744-751, 862-878). I re-ran the auditor's burst probe in my own copy: close=4008, acks=199, storedObjects=199, and peer B received 199 put broadcasts within 108 ms.

The receiver budget is a fixed 200 frames / 4 MiB per 10 s window on both clients (SyncInboundFramePolicy.kt:59-106; SyncInboundFramePolicy.swift:106-150). A 199-put burst plus any presence in the same window closes every receiver with 1008, and the sender's own budget (199 op-acks + presence) trips too. Everyone reconnects and pulls full snapshots, which feeds the S5-04 herd.

It does converge after ~ceil(N/199) cycles, via forcedLocalDiff (clearOutboundDeliveries 1189-1205). A room-wide reconnect storm from a routine KML/GPX import of a few hundred objects is high.

Mechanism confirmed.

Android: queueDelivery sends the frame and starts the retry clock at once (SyncManager.kt:1157-1187). Delays are 1/2/4/8 s with maxAttempts 5 (OutboundDeliveryTracker.kt:133, 175-188), so identical frames go out at t=0, 1, 3, 7 and 15 s. At t≈23 s nextAttempt returns null and ws.cancel() runs.

iOS is the same: task.send's completion is ignored, and the socket is cancelled after exhaustion (SyncManager.swift:2213-2248).

The relay runs a full storage.transaction for each duplicate: my vitest 'V5-09' gave 5 identical puts → 5 transactions and 5 acks.

Severity lowered to medium. Indefinite failure needs a frame (or queued backlog) whose drain takes ≳23 s, e.g. ≥~180 KB at 64 kbit/s. On links that slow, the device already cannot complete a join for any moderately sized room: Android's 20 s per-page snapshot progress timeout (V3_HANDSHAKE_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_MS, SyncManager.kt:1764) expires on a 900 KB page. The bulk-backlog variant is already covered by S5-08. Retransmitting 4 extra copies of large frames on moderate links is real waste.

Confirmed on both platforms.

Android: isSendDue requires only a fresher fix and ≥5 s since the last successful fix (UnitSyncPresenceCadence.kt:19-47; FOREGROUND_SEND_INTERVAL_SECONDS=5 at 103). There is no distance, course or speed gate, and the foreground location request runs at 1 Hz (LocationService.kt:82-88).

iOS: foreground uses kCLLocationAccuracyBest with kCLDistanceFilterNone (LocationService.swift:106-107, 122-123) plus the 5 s cadence.

Receivers keep markers for 45 s (FOREGROUND_RETENTION_SECONDS=45), so a ~20 s heartbeat while stationary would keep markers fresh at ~1/4 the traffic. This is an inefficiency with no correctness impact: medium.

Confirmed. SyncManager is a @StateObject of ContentView (ContentView.swift:514), and syncManager.peers is passed into TileMapContainer (755). Any @Published change re-evaluates the body; applyPresenceV3 on iOS sets peers, onlineMembers and chatRecipients (SyncManager.swift:4134-4165).

TileMapContainer holds non-equatable closures, so updateUIView runs every time. It rebuilds DrawingVectorShapes, decorations and handles, and calls updateOverlays → renderDrawingVectors → DrawingsOverlayView.update(shapes:). That unconditionally calls setNeedsDisplay (TileMapContainer.swift:102-139, 427-463; DrawingsOverlayView.swift:67-70), and draw() re-strokes every drawing (80+).

SwiftUI coalesces the three assignments into roughly one update per frame, so the result is one full overlay redraw per inbound presence frame, as claimed. This is a continuous CPU/GPU cost, not a correctness issue: medium.

Confirmed.

Android: SyncDialog's onClick calls manager.join (SyncDialog.kt:274). join → SyncCrypto.deriveRoomV3 (SyncManager.kt:668) → masterV3, a 210,000-iteration PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 (SyncCrypto.kt:40, 119-126), synchronously on the main-dispatcher manager.

iOS: the @MainActor join calls deriveRoomV3 (SyncManager.swift:1197), which runs CCKeyDerivationPBKDF with 210k rounds (SyncCrypto.swift:26, 97-115).

Reconnects reuse the derived keys. The cost is a single UI stall per join: low.

verify.missed:
Issues the auditor missed:

1. **iOS journal write amplification (Android/iOS divergence).** iOS observeModelRevisions loops `for id in changed { try journal.bump(id) }` (SyncManager.swift:2044). ModelRevisionJournal.bump persists the whole journal file once per id (SyncReplayState.swift:749-757). Android batches this in a single bumpAll (SyncReplayState.kt:740-748). A local KML/GPX import of N objects on iOS therefore does N full sealed rewrites of sync_model_revisions.json (O(N²)), on top of the modelHashes re-hash described in S5-03.

2. **Workers Free rows-READ quota.** Every connect lists every obj: row (index.ts:1507-1523), and Free allows 5M rows read/day. A 10k-record room exhausts it after ~500 connects/day (for example 20 members × 25 foreground returns or flaps). Snapshot reads then fail, and connects return 503 (index.ts:690-693). This is a second Free-plan DoS path, adjacent to S5-05/S5-06.

3. **S5-05 has a hostile-input angle.**
   - touchActivity runs even for loc frames that handlePresenceV3 rejects (stale counter, wrong session; index.ts:792-805 vs 1415-1424). I verified this: 5 invalid loc frames produced 5 storage.put calls.
   - Any single room member can therefore burn ~1.7M rows/day at the 200 frames/10 s limit and take down the whole account's DO writes on Free.
   - The fix is to throttle touchActivity and skip it for loc/chat frames.

4. **Android O(N) work per replay operation.**
   - roomHighWater() scans all stamps and tombstones on every canAcceptLive and every reserveLocalPut/Delete (SyncReplayState.kt:125-127, 318, 448-453).
   - persistTransaction's memorySnapshot deep-copies 7 maps per transaction (94-98), including every commitPresence.
   - Both add O(N) per operation on top of the file rewrite. Keeping a running high-water mark and using undo logs instead of full copies would remove them.

5. **Unverified: relay memory under a reconnect herd.**
   - Pages sent inside blockConcurrencyWhile are buffered by the runtime until the client drains them. A herd of slow mobile clients reconnecting to a design-max room (64 × ~13 MB) could retain far more than 128 MB of outbound data.
   - I could not determine whether workerd counts this buffer against the isolate memory limit, which would reset the DO and drop every socket.
   - A production load test with throttled clients would settle it.

6. **Minor corrections.**
   - S5-01's fsync applies to Android only. iOS uses Data.write(.atomic) with no fsync (SafeStore.swift:254-255).
   - S5-04's claim that the room nears the 30 s blockConcurrencyWhile limit is incorrect. The limit applies per call, and each call is ~1 s at 10k records.

Proof artefacts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-cbrooker-Code-TacticalMaps/d9f42208-9d3f-40e1-9b8b-49fa6c488260/scratchpad/verify-S5-efficiency/test/v5.test.ts:
- V5-05a: 35 loc frames produced 35 puts.
- V5-05b: when storage.put fails, the peer still gets the loc, the sender is closed with 1011, and a new connect gets 503.
- V5-04: a 10k-record snapshot took 915 ms, and 3 concurrent connects took 2,810 ms because they run one after another.
- V5-09: 5 duplicate puts caused 5 storage transactions.
- The auditor's burst probe, re-run in s5copy.test.ts, closed with 4008 after 199 acks, and the peer received 199 puts within 108 ms.

audit.summary:
How it works: each device derives roomId, token, roomKey and metadataKey from the join code (PBKDF2 then HMAC) and opens /v3/room/<id>. The Worker routes that to the SyncRoom Durable Object named v3:<id>. The DO pins the token hash, then streams a seq-fenced snapshot inside blockConcurrencyWhile (index.ts:686-695, 1486-1529), followed by the live hello, chat-key and loc of the other sockets. The client authenticates the snapshot and commits it to sealed SyncReplayState. It then sends a signed hello with a durable epoch, waits for hello-ack, and publishes its local diffs as signed, sealed put/del frames that carry a rid. The relay checks each stamp last-writer-wins against the stored obj: record and the room highWater ±10,000. It then stores, broadcasts, and replies op-ack or op-nack. Presence and chat are live-only, with per-socket counters kept in hibernation attachments.

Coverage today:
- Relay: 56 vitest tests, all passing in a scratch copy (9.5 s). They cover token/room binding, v2/v3 isolation, frame and byte-rate ceilings, delivery acks and nacks, v2 tombstone quota, v2 byte-chunked snapshots, hello proof and epoch replay, replacement-fence races (deterministic test seams), presence counters, the advance window, and chat v1 in depth.
- Clients: Android has 25 unit test files and iOS has 8. They test the pure helpers well (crypto vectors, replay state, delivery tracker, v2 snapshot gate, cadence, backoff, endpoint policy) and share the fixtures sync_protocol_v3, tacmap_chat_v1, presence_accuracy_v3, local_store_name_v1 and malicious_frames.
- Missing: no deterministic test of either client's SyncManager state machine (neither platform has a transport seam). No relay eviction, alarm or limit tests. Cross-platform live interop checks chat only.

What I added in the scratch copy (7 relay tests, audit-sync/s6-audit.test.ts, 63/63 passing):
- Solid: hibernation eviction keeps session, presence and chat replay state. A randomized multi-actor fuzz converges: relay storage equals every client's fold and the late-joiner snapshot.
- Defects proven: counter-window lockout after idle expiry, a stale nack in ordinary edit races, one durable write per presence frame with the socket closed on write failure, and bulk-publish cut-off at 200 frames.
- Prototype harness (audit-sync/v3-soak.mjs): real v3 crypto, self-tested against the shared fixture. Run against wrangler dev with 6 clients for 30 s and a relay restart at 15 s: it converged, with 1,089 acks (36/s), 25 stale nacks and 20 reconnects. Fan-out latency p50/p95/p99 was 3/9/11 ms locally, and the restart took the relay down for 808 ms.

findings.title: Untested relay idle-expiry wipe locks out returning clients (counter-window reconnect loop), resurrects deletes, and leaves a permanent rollback warning
findings.description:
alarm() (index.ts:834-847) calls storage.deleteAll() once a room has had no sockets for 7 days. That removes meta:highWater, meta:seq, meta:auth, every actor: pin and every obj: record and tombstone. Clients keep localCounter, stamps, tombstones and lastSnapshotSeq in sealed replay state. No test on any platform covers this, although runDurableObjectAlarm is available.

I proved the relay half in the scratch vitest: after an 8-day idle alarm, a returning actor whose counter had legitimately reached 18,000 sends put 18,001 and gets op-nack {code:"counter-window", retry:false}. The cause is that highWater reset to 0 and the relay accepts at most 0+10,000 (index.ts:1195).

Both clients treat counter-window as non-retryable and cancel the socket (Android SyncManager.kt:2063-2065, iOS SyncManager.swift:3091-3093). That leads to a reconnect loop:
- The rejected op stays in the tracker, so clearOutboundDeliveries(markForReconciliation=true) puts it in forcedLocalDiff (SyncManager.kt:1195).
- After hello-ack it is re-sent with the same too-high stamp, because recoverableLocalPut returns the reserved stamp (SyncReplayState.kt:435-441; iOS recoveryStamp at SyncManager.swift:2322).
- The backoff is reset at every hello-ack (SyncManager.kt:2236, SyncManager.swift:3552).
- Result: roughly 1 s cycles of connect, full snapshot, durable hello-epoch write, nack and cancel, forever. Every device behind the same IP also burns CONN_LIMITER's 60/min.

Second consequence: tombstones authored by absent actors are never re-published, because recoverableLocalDeletes only covers the local actor (SyncReplayState.kt:443-448). A stale returning device re-stamps a deleted object below the tombstone counter. The wiped relay accepts it, but peers holding the tombstone reject it (canAcceptLive/beatsCurrent, :124-134). The result is permanent divergence between those peers and the relay plus late joiners.

Third consequence: seq restarts at 0, which is below lastSnapshotSeq. Every connect then raises a SECURITY rollback warning (Android :1904-1910, iOS :3478) until the relay's seq exceeds the old value. ADR-001 §9-10 does not define a relay reset.
findings.failure_scenario:
A unit uses its room for weekend exercises. After 8 idle days the DO alarm wipes the room. Device A's local Lamport counter is 18,000 after months of drawing edits. It reconnects and gets an empty snapshot (seq 0), so the user sees a security rollback warning. A's first edit reserves 18,001, the relay nacks counter-window, and A cancels, reconnects in about 1 s and re-sends the same stamp. This repeats indefinitely, draining battery and data and never syncing.

Separately: C was offline when D (who has since left) deleted waypoint X. C comes back after the wipe and re-publishes X at counter 300. The relay accepts it, but A still holds D's tombstone at 500 and rejects it. A and every new joiner permanently disagree about X.
findings.suggested_fix:
1. On expiry, delete obj: and actor: records but retain meta:seq and meta:highWater (and optionally meta:auth), which costs 2-3 rows per dead room. Add an expired/roomGeneration marker to snapshot-begin so clients can tell a benign reset from a rollback attack. On that marker, clients republish their own objects and re-issue every retained tombstone as their own delete, stamped above the tombstone counter.
2. Independently, never tear down the socket on counter-window, stale or not-found. Mark the op failed once, surface a single non-security notice, and do not loop.
3. Document relay reset in ADR-001 §9-10.
findings.proving_test:
Scratch vitest (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-cbrooker-Code-TacticalMaps/d9f42208-9d3f-40e1-9b8b-49fa6c488260/scratchpad/audit-sync/s6-audit.test.ts, 'idle-expiry deleteAll resets highWater so a returning veteran client is locked out by counter-window'). It back-dates meta:lastActivity, calls runDurableObjectAlarm(stub), then asserts that highWater, auth, obj and actor are gone, that snapshot-begin has seq 0 and highWater 0, and that put(18001) gets an op-nack with counter-window. It currently passes, which demonstrates the bug. After the fix, the same test must see an ack, seq ≥ 2, and an expiry marker.

Client script tests (with the S6-02 seam): feed snapshot(seq 0) then an op-nack counter-window, and assert no socket cancel and no reconnect within 30 s.

Harness: v3-soak.mjs --wipe (stop wrangler, delete --persist-to, restart) plus --late-returner. Assert convergence and that reconnects are bounded.

findings.title: Client SyncManager state machines have no transport seam and no deterministic tests; every nack, reconnect, snapshot and background path is reachable only through opt-in live runs
findings.description:
Android hard-wires `private val webSocketTransport = SyncWebSocketTransport()` (SyncManager.kt:254). iOS hard-wires URLSessionWebSocketTask (SyncManager.swift:762-764, 1655), and all its handlers are private (handleMessage 2905, handleParsedMessageV3 3362, applyDeliveryNack 3054, and others). So neither platform can feed frames into the real 3.7k-line (Android) or 4.2k-line (iOS) manager.

Existing tests reach only pure helpers. SyncManagerLiveSessionTest only exercises acceptedV3Departure. The iOS tests build SyncManager only for config and identity checks. CI runs unit tests only.

Paths with no test at all:
- snapshot-begin/page/end sequencing through production code
- the fixture's 'reject-entire-snapshot' duplicate-ID policy (only the constant is asserted, relay.test.ts:658)
- hello-ack gating and 20 s/30 s handshake timeouts
- op-nack reactions (stale, counter-window, quota, session-*)
- ack-loss retry timers (1/2/4/8 s)
- backoff reset at hello-ack
- background frame drop and foreground re-snapshot
- the chat-key lifecycle
- pending-model repair under live traffic

The defects in S6-01, S6-03, S6-04, S6-05 and S6-07 all sit in these paths, and the two platforms can drift here without any failing test.
findings.failure_scenario: A change to Android's applyDeliveryNack (for example adding a code to the cancel set) or to iOS snapshot handling ships with green CI and only shows up as a reconnect loop or divergence in the field. Today both platforms reconnect on every stale nack (S6-03), and nothing would catch a fix on one platform only.
findings.suggested_fix:
Add a transport factory seam on both platforms:
- Android: a constructor parameter `socketFactory: (url, headers, SyncWebSocketListener) -> SyncWebSocket`, defaulting to SyncWebSocketTransport::newWebSocket. The interface already exists (SyncWebSocketTransport.kt:23-35).
- iOS: `protocol SyncSocket { send; receive; cancel(with:) }` wrapping URLSessionWebSocketTask, injected through init. Also inject clocks and delay schedulers.

Build an in-memory scripted relay on each platform, driven by one shared fixture, testdata/sync_session_scripts.json. Each script is a sequence of expected-outbound patterns, inbound frames, and expected state (status, store contents, lastError kind, reconnect count, frames sent). Both suites run every script, the way the crypto vectors are shared today. Initial scripts: happy-join, duplicate-id-snapshot, stale-nack-no-reconnect, counter-window-after-wipe, ack-loss-retry, background-then-foreground, bulk-publish-paced, and the malicious corpus per phase.
findings.proving_test:
Script 'stale-nack-no-reconnect':
1. Connect with an empty snapshot and hello-ack.
2. Edit waypoint X, so the client emits put 5:A.
3. Inject put 5:B for X, then op-nack {code:stale, retry:false} for A's rid.
4. Assert status stays CONNECTED, zero new sockets are created, lastError is not SECURITY, and the model equals B's content.

Today this fails on both platforms (Android SyncManager.kt:2063-2065, iOS SyncManager.swift:3091-3093).

findings.title: Losing an ordinary LWW race raises a SECURITY error, tears down the socket and re-downloads the whole room
findings.description:
The relay nacks {code:"stale", retry:false} whenever the incoming stamp is not newer than the stored one (index.ts:1192). This includes the normal concurrent case: two devices that saw the same high-water both reserve counter c for the same object, and the higher actorId wins.

The relay sends the winner's broadcast before the nack on the same socket, so the loser already has the converged state. Even so, both clients map stale to reportError(kind SECURITY) and cancel the socket (Android SyncManager.kt:2051-2065, iOS SyncManager.swift:3072-3093). That forces a reconnect with a new session domain, a durable hello-epoch write on the relay, a full snapshot, and a chat and presence reset.

Proven:
- Scratch vitest: the loser receives [put from B, op-nack stale retry:false].
- Soak prototype (6 clients, 24 shared objects): about 2.2% of writes were stale.
- Emulating the apps (--app-nack-reconnect) adds one reconnect per stale nack, and snapshot bytes rose from 254 KB to 464 KB in 30 s even for a 24-object room. That cost scales with room size (48 MB measured for 5,000 records, see S6-12).

The only nack test on the clients is a tracker unit test using "quota".
findings.failure_scenario: Two operators adjust the same phase line within a second of each other. The losing phone shows a security warning ('relay rejected an out-of-date change'), drops presence and chat for a moment, and re-downloads the whole room. With several editors on shared drawings this happens repeatedly, and every drag race costs a full snapshot on mobile data.
findings.suggested_fix:
Treat stale and not-found as an expected LWW outcome:
- Drop the pending op and keep the socket.
- Do not report SECURITY. Optionally show a quiet 'overwritten by X' toast.
- Only if the local replay state holds no stamp newer than the rejected one (a true anomaly), schedule a snapshot resync.
- Keep teardown for session-replaced, session-mismatch and hello-required only.

Apply the same change on both platforms in the same PR, and add a shared script test.
findings.proving_test:
Scratch vitest 'an ordinary concurrent same-counter edit yields a non-retryable stale nack to the LWW loser' (audit-sync/s6-audit.test.ts) proves the relay side.

Client: the S6-02 script 'stale-nack-no-reconnect'.

Harness regression metric: in v3-soak.mjs with app behaviour, reconnects must equal injected flaps plus restarts. Today they also include one per stale nack.

findings.title: Chat sent to a peer whose phone is locked in background-presence mode is acked 'Routed' and silently lost
findings.description:
With background location sharing enabled, both apps keep the already-authenticated socket open when the app locks or backgrounds:
- Android: enterBackgroundPresenceOnly, SyncManager.kt:387-417.
- iOS: updateLifecycle, SyncManager.swift:1003-1007.

Both clear the X25519 chat key locally (clearChatTransport / clearChatSessionSecrets) and then discard every inbound frame before parsing (Android :1797, iOS :1720). Neither sends anything to the relay: there is no chat-key withdrawal frame in the protocol.

The relay attachment therefore still holds chatKey. routeChat still treats the socket as a live, chat-capable recipient for both room and direct messages (index.ts:1320, 1328-1330) and sends chat-ack, so the sender marks the message Routed. Senders also keep offering the locked unit as a direct recipient, because no leave is broadcast.

This breaks ADR-004's own required tests: item 5 ('offline, replaced, and stale-key targets produce a failure') and item 8 (lock lifecycle). There is no mailbox, so the message is gone. No test on any platform covers chat to a backgrounded peer.
findings.failure_scenario: A team leader sends a direct 'RTB now' to a patrol member whose phone is locked in a pocket with background location on (the normal field posture). The leader's app shows Routed. The member's app drops the frame; on unlock it reconnects with a fresh snapshot and has no record of the message.
findings.suggested_fix:
Add a socket-bound `{"t":"chat-key-revoke","cv":1}`. The relay clears attachment.chatKey, chatCounter and lastChat, and broadcasts a signed-session-scoped chat withdrawal that peers use to remove the recipient. Clients send it before entering background presence (or after, in the same main-thread turn, before any loc).

Alternative: rotate to a presence-only session (a new hello and sd with no chat-key) when backgrounding. This could share the quiet-subscription mode proposed in S6-05.
findings.proving_test:
Relay vitest: using openChatPair, B sends the revoke. A's direct chat to (B, sd, kid) must get chat-nack recipient_offline, and A's room chat must not reach B.

Client script test: after enterBackgroundPresenceOnly (Android) or updateLifecycle(foregroundReady:false, backgroundPresenceEnabled:true) (iOS), the next outbound frame must be the revoke.

Live interop (S6-10): lock the iOS simulator with location-always granted, have Android send a direct message, and expect a failure state rather than ROUTED.

findings.title: Background presence-only sockets still receive the room's whole fan-out; the radio stays busy and a busy room trips the client's own receive budget
findings.description:
The opt-in background mode is built around a 1-60 minute send cadence (default 15 min), but the socket stays fully subscribed. broadcast() sends every peer's loc (every 5 s per foreground peer, SyncManager.swift:573), every put/del and room chat to every socket (index.ts:1556-1562). The locked device receives each frame and throws it away (Android :1797, iOS :1720).

With 10 foreground peers that is about 2 frames/s (~0.5-1 KB each after AEAD and base64), roughly 4-7 MB per hour of useless downlink. The cellular radio never drops to idle, which defeats the battery design.

The discarded frames are still counted by the LIVE receive budget (200 frames/10 s, Android :103-105, iOS :111-113; Android admits before the background drop at :1779-1797). A busy room therefore makes the locked device close its own socket with 1008. Background presence then ends silently until the next foreground: Android calls backgroundTransportEnded, and on iOS the handleDisconnect reconnect gate is closed.

Nothing measures inbound traffic to a background session.
findings.failure_scenario: On a 6-hour patrol, 12 of 15 team members have the map open. The 3 members with locked phones and 15-minute background presence still receive about 2.4 location frames/s the whole time. Their batteries drain as if the app were in the foreground. When someone publishes a batch of drawings, their sockets hit the 200-frame budget and close, so their positions vanish from everyone's map.
findings.suggested_fix:
Add a quiet or presence-only subscription:
- A signed flag on hello, or a socket-bound {"t":"subscribe","live":false} frame.
- The relay then skips that socket in broadcast() and routeChat, still accepts its loc, and still sends it leave and hello for its own session.
- Clients send it before going egress-only. The foreground return already reconnects with a full snapshot.
- Also exempt frames discarded in background from the live budget, or apply a separate larger background budget.
findings.proving_test:
Harness: v3-soak.mjs --background 2 marks two clients as egress-only (loc every 60 s, no consumption) and asserts inbound bytes/frames to them over 10 min. Today that is about peers × 120 loc frames plus all puts; after the fix it should be about 0.

Relay vitest: after the quiet flag, a peer's put/loc/chat is not delivered to the quiet socket, while the quiet socket's loc still reaches others.

findings.title: Every presence, chat and put frame performs a durable storage write, and a write failure closes the live socket (self-DoS on the advertised Workers Free plan)
findings.description:
processWebSocketMessage calls touchActivity() after every non-ping frame inside its try block (index.ts:805). touchActivity does storage.put("meta:lastActivity") plus getAlarm (:1564-1568). The catch at :806-809 closes the socket with 1011 'storage unavailable'. The post-snapshot touchActivity in fetch (:689) turns a failure into a 503 for new connections.

Proven in the scratch vitest: 20 loc frames produced 20 storage.put calls, and an injected put failure on loc closed the sender with 1011.

Cloudflare's Workers Free plan, which wrangler.jsonc says the relay supports, allows 100,000 rows written per day per account, and setAlarm counts as a row. At the 5 s foreground cadence each device writes 17,280 rows/day from presence alone. About 6 devices running all day, or 15 devices during an 8-hour exercise plus about 5 rows per put, exhaust the daily quota. After that every loc closes its socket, and every reconnect gets 503 until the quota resets.

On the paid plan it is pure cost: about 5M rows/month for a 10-device room. The idle TTL is 7 days, so minute-level precision is plenty. None of this is tested or measured.
findings.failure_scenario: A self-hosted relay on the free plan (as the README invites) supports a 15-person exercise. Around midday the account passes 100k rows written. Every presence frame now gets its socket closed with 1011, every reconnect returns 503 'Snapshot unavailable', and Unit Sync is dead for everyone until the daily reset. The apps report network errors, not quota exhaustion.
findings.suggested_fix:
- Keep lastActivity in memory and write it at most once every 10-60 minutes, and on the last close. While sockets are connected, the alarm already reschedules itself (index.ts:836-838).
- Never fail a socket on activity-bookkeeping errors: emit a metric and continue.
- Add a storage_row_writes metric so self-hosters can see the budget.
findings.proving_test:
Scratch vitest 'every presence frame performs a durable write, and a write failure closes the live socket' (audit-sync/s6-audit.test.ts) passes today.

Invert it after the fix:
- At most 1 storage.put per 60 s of continuous presence.
- An injected put failure during loc does not close the socket.

Harness: add a relay debug metric for row writes and assert rows/min ≤ puts×5 + 1 over a 30-minute soak.

findings.title: Unpaced bulk publish (import, first join with a pre-existing map, post-wipe re-upload) is cut off by the relay at 200 frames and pushes every peer past its 200-frame live budget
findings.description:
syncLocalStateV3 sends a signed put for every changed object in one loop, with no pacing (Android :1310-1323, iOS :2288-2299). The only outbound bound is 16 MB of queued bytes. The relay allows 200 messages per 10 s per socket and closes with 4008 at the 201st (index.ts:862-878). Each client allows 200 application frames per 10 s in total after CONNECTED.

Proven in the scratch vitest: 250 back-to-back puts produce 200 acks, then a 4008 close. The peer received 200 puts within 133 ms, so the next frame of any kind within 10 s (a peer's loc, or the cut-off sender's reconnect hello) makes every peer close with 1008. They all reconnect and take full snapshots. The sender retries about every 1 s with the next 200.

The trigger is ordinary use:
- importing a mission file of more than about 200 objects
- deleting a layer with more than 200 drawings
- a device joining a room with more than 200 existing local objects, all of which are pushed on first join
- the re-upload after S6-01

No client or relay test covers bulk publishing.
findings.failure_scenario: A platoon sergeant joins the unit room on a phone that already holds a 600-object route and overlay plan. The phone publishes 200, is closed with 4008, reconnects, publishes 200 more, and so on. Each burst knocks all 14 other phones offline with 1008 and each of them re-downloads the room, three times in about 30 s. On a shared NAT the reconnect burst also runs into CONN_LIMITER's 60 connections/min.
findings.suggested_fix:
- Client: pace outbound frames with a token bucket of about 150 frames per 10 s, including loc and hello. Send in stable order and let acks drive the next window.
- Relay: return a retryable op-nack {code:"rate", retry:true} instead of closing for frames that are otherwise valid; keep the close for abuse (for example more than 2× the budget).
- Make the client's LIVE budget consistent with the relay's aggregate fan-out: count frames per sender actor, or raise the aggregate limit and enforce a per-room fan-out cap at the relay.
findings.proving_test:
Scratch vitest 'an unpaced 250-object publish is cut off by the relay at 200 frames and floods peers past the client 200-frame live budget' passes today and demonstrates the bug.

After the fix:
- Client script 'bulk-publish-paced' imports 1,000 objects and asserts the socket is never closed, peer inbound frames stay ≤ 200 per 10 s, and all 1,000 are acked.
- Harness v3-soak.mjs --bulk 1000 asserts zero 1008/4008 closes and convergence.

findings.title: Relay hibernation/eviction, alarm, connection cap, production rate limits, v3 snapshot paging and accounting migration have no tests
findings.description:
relay.test.ts imports only env, SELF and runInDurableObject. @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers 0.22.0 also ships evictDurableObject(stub, {webSockets: 'hibernate'|'close'}), evictAllDurableObjects, abortAllDurableObjects and runDurableObjectAlarm, but none are used.

I added an eviction test. The core hibernation paths are solid: session binding, presence and chat replay counters, live snapshot (hello, chat-key, loc) and leave-on-close all survive.

Still untested:
- MAX_CONNECTIONS (the 65th connection should get 503).
- Production CONN_LIMITER 60/min and ROOM_LIMITER 10/min per IP. vitest.config.ts overrides both to 10,000, and a unit behind one NAT that reconnects after a deploy is the realistic case.
- v3 snapshot paging: the byte-pages test uses v2 sockets (relay.test.ts:559-573).
- The invariant that a record at CT_MAX 700,000 fits in a 900,000-byte frame. If it didn't, one record would make the room unjoinable (index.ts:1515).
- ensureV3Accounting for pre-ADR records without sd (the +80 formula).
- Alarm rescheduling while sockets are live.
- webSocketError aborting a queue.
- v3 quota exhaustion. Tombstones are never garbage-collected, so a room with object churn hits 10,000 records permanently while it stays active.
findings.failure_scenario:
A future change moves a field from the attachment into instance memory. Hibernation drops it, presence replay protection silently resets after the DO sleeps, and no test notices because nothing evicts the object.

Or: a 30-device unit on one base Wi-Fi reconnects after a relay deploy and hits CONN_LIMITER 429s. Nobody has seen how the apps behave under that, because tests never run the production limits.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the vitest cases listed in S6-11 (4). Add a second vitest project (vitest.limits.config.ts) that keeps wrangler.jsonc's ratelimits so the 429 paths are covered. Pin the constants invariant CT_MAX + max record overhead < SNAPSHOT_FRAME_BYTES in a test.
findings.proving_test: Scratch vitest 'keeps session binding, presence and chat replay counters, and live snapshot across evictDurableObject' (passes). New tests: 65 sockets → the last gets 503; a v3 room with 2 × 500 KB records pages into 2 frames ≤ 900,000 bytes; one CT_MAX record fits one frame; under limits config the 61st upgrade in 60 s → 429; a legacy record without sd migrates to exact byte accounting; with a socket connected runDurableObjectAlarm reschedules and deletes nothing.

findings.title: The hostile-input corpus never reaches production handlers; Android's version test re-implements the parser; there are no v3 hostile cases
findings.description:
malicious_frames.json says both platforms must drop each frame 'without state mutation, crash, or hang'. The tests don't check that:
- Android versionParsingRejectsAllMaliciousValues copies strictVersion's logic into the test ('simulate what SyncManager.strictVersion does'), so deleting SyncManager.strictVersion would not fail it. noFrameCrashesJsonParsing parses with kotlinx Json, not the org.json JSONObject that production uses (org.json is available as a test dependency).
- iOS calls the production strictJSONInteger, but neither platform drives frames through handleMessage in any connection phase.
- The relay does not load the corpus at all.
- All 25 cases are v2-shaped. There are no v3 hostile cases.

Missing v3 cases:
- duplicate wire IDs in a snapshot (the reject-entire-snapshot policy is only asserted as a constant)
- snapshot-end with a mismatched seq
- pages after more:false
- a snapshot page before snapshot-begin
- hello-ack for the wrong sd or vs
- put or loc before hello-ack
- op-ack with the wrong cth
- leave for an unknown session
- chat for a stale kid
findings.failure_scenario: A refactor of Android's handleMessageV3 or strictVersion accepts a fractional 'v', or applies a snapshot with a duplicated wire ID. The corpus tests still pass because they never call production code. A hostile relay or room member can then corrupt replay state.
findings.suggested_fix:
Once the S6-02 seam exists:
- Replay every corpus frame through the production handler in the CONNECTING, SNAPSHOTTING, awaiting-hello-ack and CONNECTED phases. Assert that store, replay state, peers and lastError are unchanged and that the close code is as expected.
- Add a 'phase' field and the v3 cases to malicious_frames.json.
- In relay.test.ts, replay the corpus on v2 and v3 sockets and assert no broadcast and no storage change.
- Delete the reimplemented logic in the Android test.
findings.proving_test: Mutation check: stub SyncManager.strictVersion to accept every value and confirm the new corpus test fails (today it still passes). Snapshot duplicate-ID script: two snapshot items with the same id must reject the whole snapshot, commit nothing, and produce a SECURITY error on both platforms.

findings.title: Cross-platform live interop only checks chat; iOS↔Android object and presence convergence is never asserted, and nothing runs in CI
findings.description:
The only live cross-platform checks:
- The Android instrumented chat round-trip.
- The iOS testLiveProductionHandshakeWhenRelayIsProvided. With TACMAP_LIVE_EMIT_OBJECT=1 it adds one waypoint (:2718-2723), but nothing on Android asserts receipt.

Not exercised end to end: waypoint, drawing and delete exchange; the receiver fixed-point model hash (expectedModelHash) across platforms; presence decode, accuracy and retention; relay restart; network faults; backgrounding. Wire compatibility rests only on the shared vectors.

Dev plumbing constraints:
- DEBUG builds accept ws:// only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (Android RelayEndpointPolicy.kt:80-88 with allowInsecureLoopback=BuildConfig.DEBUG; iOS :21-27, 67-78). 10.0.2.2 is rejected, so the emulator needs adb reverse.
- Android uses raw Java-WebSocket sockets and ships no network_security_config, so cleartext loopback works.
- There is no relay-URL UI (by design, per UnitSyncSettingsContractTest), so apps can only be pointed at a relay through the test entry points.
findings.failure_scenario: An iOS exporter change alters a drawing's GeoJSON so that Android re-exports it differently. Android then treats every inbound iOS drawing as locally diverged and re-publishes it at a new stamp, and the two phones ping-pong the object. No test anywhere puts the two platforms on the same relay with objects.
findings.suggested_fix:
Plan (3). Relay and connectivity:
- `cd sync && npx wrangler dev --port 8791 --ip 127.0.0.1 --persist-to .wrangler/interop`.
- Android emulator: `adb reverse tcp:8791 tcp:8791`, relay ws://127.0.0.1:8791. The iOS simulator shares host loopback, so it uses the same URL.

Running each side:
- Android: `./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest -Pandroid.testInstrumentationRunnerArguments.class=com.tacmap.sync.<Test> -Pandroid.testInstrumentationRunnerArguments.TACMAP_LIVE_RELAY=ws://127.0.0.1:8791 -Pandroid.testInstrumentationRunnerArguments.TACMAP_LIVE_JOIN_CODE=3:<code> -Pandroid.testInstrumentationRunnerArguments.TACMAP_CHAT_INTEROP_RUN_ID=<id>`.
- iOS: `TEST_RUNNER_TACMAP_LIVE_RELAY=ws://127.0.0.1:8791 TEST_RUNNER_TACMAP_LIVE_JOIN_CODE=3:<code> TEST_RUNNER_TACMAP_CHAT_INTEROP_RUN_ID=<id> TEST_RUNNER_TACMAP_LIVE_EMIT_OBJECT=1 xcodebuild test ... -only-testing:TacticalMapsTests/SyncProtocolV3Tests/testLiveProductionHandshakeWhenRelayIsProvided`. xcodebuild strips the TEST_RUNNER_ prefix.

New tests, in the same sandboxed style:
- androidTest SyncObjectLiveInteropTest and iOS testLiveObjectAndPresenceInterop.
- Each side creates a run-id-tagged waypoint, polygon and line, edits one, and deletes one. It then waits for the other side's set and asserts equality by (local UUID, production-exporter fixed-point hash) plus tombstone absence.
- Presence: shareLocation=true with simulated fixes (`xcrun simctl location booted set -33.8688,151.2093`; `adb emu geo fix 151.2093 -33.8688`). Assert the peer marker and callsign appear within 10 s and clear on explicit leave.

Orchestration (scripts/sync_live_interop.sh):
- Run both sides concurrently with one join code and run ID.
- Add v3-soak.mjs as a headless third member (same derive()) that decrypts and verifies both apps' records and serves as the relay-truth oracle.

Fault steps:
- Restart wrangler with the same persist dir.
- Route both apps through a node TCP fault proxy on 127.0.0.1:8793 (latency, RST, half-open).
- Background iOS (`xcrun simctl privacy booted grant location-always <bundle>` then `xcrun simctl launch booted com.apple.Preferences`) and Android (`adb shell input keyevent KEYCODE_HOME`) to cover S6-04 and S6-05.
- Delete the persist dir between restarts to cover S6-01.

Run nightly on the macOS runner ios.yml already uses, with reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner.
findings.proving_test: SyncObjectLiveInteropTest (Android) and testLiveObjectAndPresenceInterop (iOS) must both pass concurrently against one wrangler dev room. The node observer must report an identical record set before and after a mid-run relay restart.

findings.title: No executable soak, property or restart harness exists; a working prototype and a concrete plan are provided
findings.description:
There is no multi-client randomized traffic test, no disconnect/restart soak, and no latency or throughput or cost number anywhere in the repo. The only relay-facing script, scripts/sync_push_situation.mjs, speaks v2 and points at the production relay URL.

I built and ran a prototype (scratchpad/audit-sync/v3-soak.mjs, 202 lines, using only node:crypto and sync/node_modules/ws 8.21). Before sending traffic it self-tests the v3 derivation, wire ID and object_put preimage against testdata/sync_protocol_v3.json.

Results against wrangler dev:
- 6 clients, 30 s, relay restart at 15 s: converged; 1,089 acks (36/s); 25 stale; 20 reconnects; 0 HTTP 429s; fan-out p50/p95/p99 3/9/11 ms; 808 ms relay downtime; 254 KB of snapshots in total.
- With --app-nack-reconnect: one extra reconnect per stale nack, and snapshot bytes 464 KB.

A vitest-level randomized property test (4 generated Ed25519 actors, 150 ops, mulberry32 seeds, 91-98 stale per run) also passes: relay storage equals every client's fold and the late-joiner snapshot.
findings.failure_scenario: Convergence and efficiency regressions (reconnect storms, snapshot amplification, rate-limit cut-offs, relay-reset handling) are invisible to CI. S6-01, S6-03, S6-05, S6-06 and S6-07 were all found only by constructing these scenarios by hand.
findings.suggested_fix:
(1) Harness: promote the prototype to sync/test/soak/v3-soak.mjs with an `npm run soak` script.
- Client model mirrors the apps: counter = max(local, seen)+1; a fresh sd and hello epoch+1 per connection; unacked ops re-signed for the new sd with the same stamp after hello-ack; stale and not-found dropped; --app-nack-reconnect emulates current app behaviour.
- Workload per 50 ms tick: 1/3 put or del over a 24-object pool (1/6 of those deletes), 1/10 loc, 1/400 abrupt terminate(); exponential backoff.
- Oracle: after quiesce, a fresh observer's snapshot fold is the truth. Every client's LWW replica must match it on (id, vs, deleted, sha256(ct)). Exit 1 and print the seed otherwise.
- Metrics JSON: latency percentiles, acks/s, nack histogram, reconnects, 429s, per-reconnect snapshot bytes, wire bytes in and out.
- Run: `cd sync && node test/soak/v3-soak.mjs --spawn . --persist .wrangler/soak --relay ws://127.0.0.1:8792 --clients 6 --seconds 30 --restart-at 15 --seed 11`. It spawns `wrangler dev --port 8792 --ip 127.0.0.1 --persist-to ...`.
- Scenario flags to add: --wipe, --late-returner, --bulk N, --background K, --clients 65, --flaky (node TCP proxy that injects latency, RST and half-open), and --hours 8 (reporting a relay debug metric for storage rows written, plus memory).
- The local limiter never tripped in my run (about 66 connects/min under the key 'unknown'), so assert limiter semantics in vitest instead (S6-08).
- Nightly workflow .github/workflows/sync-soak.yml: 50 seeds × 30 s plus one 30-minute soak. Consider fast-check as a devDependency for shrinking.

(2) Restart and eviction mid-traffic:
- Harness --restart-at: SIGINT wrangler dev and reuse the persist dir. All sockets drop and in-memory queues and fence counters are lost while storage is kept, which models a deploy.
- Vitest: evictDurableObject(stub) and evictDurableObject(stub, {webSockets:'close'}) between frames; abortAllDurableObjects() while a put transaction or hello registration is held open by the existing helloHandshakeDelayMsForTests seam; runDurableObjectAlarm after back-dating meta:lastActivity, and again with a live socket.

(4) Vitest additions:
- The 7 scratch tests in audit-sync/s6-audit.test.ts (expiry lockout, LWW-loser nack, eviction continuity, randomized convergence, per-frame write plus fail-closed, 5,000-record snapshot measurement, bulk-publish cut-off). Invert the bug-proving ones once fixed.
- 65th socket → 503.
- A limits project with production ratelimits.
- v3 paging with a CT_MAX record.
- ensureV3Accounting migration.
- malicious_frames.json replay on v2 and v3 sockets.
- Relay cross-actor tie-break from fixture version_stamp.comparison_cases.
- webSocketError queue abort.
- v3 quota exhaustion from tombstones.
findings.proving_test:
`node /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-cbrooker-Code-TacticalMaps/d9f42208-9d3f-40e1-9b8b-49fa6c488260/scratchpad/audit-sync/v3-soak.mjs --relay ws://127.0.0.1:8792 --clients 6 --seconds 30 --spawn <copy of sync> --persist <dir> --restart-at 15 --seed 11` exits 0 and prints converged:true.

Copy audit-sync/s6-audit.test.ts into sync/test/ and run `npx vitest run`: 63/63 pass today.

findings.title: Every reconnect and every foreground return re-downloads the entire room; the cost is unmeasured and there is no resume
findings.description:
sendSnapshot always streams every obj: record, inside blockConcurrencyWhile. Clients never send lastSnapshotSeq, and records don't carry per-record seq, so the relay cannot send a delta.

By design, iOS reconnects with a full snapshot on every foreground return (SyncManager.swift:963-964, 992-993), and Android does the same through prepareForForegroundUnlock and attachForegroundStores. Network flaps and S6-03 stale nacks add more full snapshots.

Measured in miniflare: a 5,000-record room with about 7 KB per record (close to the 50 MB quota) produced 48.3 MB in 56 frames per connect, about 0.6 s locally. Relay-side memory and the room-wide concurrency stall under simultaneous reconnects (after a deploy) are unmeasured. No test bounds bytes per reconnect.
findings.failure_scenario: A user who checks the map 40 times during a patrol re-downloads a 3 MB room 40 times (120 MB). After a relay deploy, 30 devices reconnect within about 1 s, and each full snapshot blocks the DO's input gate while the next one waits.
findings.suggested_fix:
- Store the mutation seq on each obj: record.
- Let the client pass since=<lastSnapshotSeq> (in the upgrade headers or the first frame). The relay streams only records with seq > since, including tombstones, whenever since is at or above a retained compaction floor.
- Keep full snapshots for new, expired or reset rooms.
- Clients already authenticate each record, so omission risk is the same as today.
- Track the bytes-per-reconnect metric in the soak harness.
findings.proving_test: Scratch vitest 'measures full-snapshot bytes/time for a near-quota room' prints s6_snapshot_bytes=48,262,142 with 5,000 records. Harness: after the fix, bytes per reconnect for an unchanged room of 5,000 records must be under 10 KB. An iOS foreground cycle must not transfer more than the delta.

findings.title: The v3 fixture generator (gen_v3_fixtures.mjs) is not in the repo
findings.description: sync_protocol_v3.json says it was 'Generated by gen_v3_fixtures.mjs', but `git ls-files` contains no such script (and no chat or presence generator). New normative cases can't be added reproducibly. Examples: a relay-reset marker, a chat-key revoke frame, a quiet subscription, v3 hostile frames, and session scripts. Vectors would have to be hand-edited, which testdata/README.md forbids in spirit. The soak prototype had to re-implement derivation and preimages and self-check them against the JSON.
findings.failure_scenario: A fix for S6-01 or S6-04 adds new signed frames. Someone hand-crafts the vectors on one platform and copies them, so the 'independent implementation' check is lost and the platforms can drift while tests stay green.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit the generators under testdata/tools/ (node:crypto only). Add a CI step to sync.yml that regenerates the fixtures and fails on any diff. Reuse the generator's primitives in sync/test/soak/v3-soak.mjs.
findings.proving_test: CI job: `node testdata/tools/gen_v3_fixtures.mjs --check` exits 0 on the current JSON and non-zero when any vector byte is altered.

verdicts.reasoning:
I re-ran the auditor's scratch test in my own copy (verify-S6-tests-plan/test/s6-audit.test.ts) and it passes (7/7). After alarm() at index.ts:834-847 calls deleteAll(), snapshot-begin reports seq 0 and highWater 0, and put(18001) gets op-nack counter-window with retry:false (index.ts:1193-1195).

I traced the client side myself.
- Android: reserveLocalPut/reserveLocalDelete use max(localCounter, local roomHighWater)+1, and the local counter survives the wipe (SyncReplayState.kt:324-356). iOS does the same through reserveNextCounter = localCounter+1 (SyncReplayState.swift:199-204).
- OutboundDeliveryTracker.reject keeps the op with its rejectionCode instead of removing it (OutboundDeliveryTracker.kt reject()).
- applyDeliveryNack reports SECURITY and cancels the socket for counter-window (SyncManager.kt:2046-2067; iOS 3054-3095).
- onClosed calls clearOutboundDeliveries(markForReconciliation=true), which puts the op in forcedLocalDiff (SyncManager.kt:1011, 1189-1205), then reconnects after nextDelayMs.
- The backoff was reset at the previous hello-ack (SyncManager.kt:2236; iOS 3552), so the delay is about 1 s ±20%.
- After the next hello-ack, recoverableLocalPut returns the same reserved stamp (SyncReplayState.kt:435-441), so the same 18001 frame is re-sent. recoverableLocalDeletes re-sends every own tombstone at its old stamp as well, because an empty snapshot confirms none of them.
- Because detachMissionStateForKeyLock clears lastContent (SyncManager.kt:451), any foreground return re-diffs every local object. A veteran device therefore enters the loop without making a new edit.

The loop is effectively bounded only by CONN_LIMITER 60/min per IP (index.ts:585-590).

The rollback warning is also real. lastSnapshotSeq = max(old, new) (SyncReplayState.kt:185, 202) and the check at SyncManager.kt:1904-1910 / iOS :3478 re-raises a SECURITY issue every connection until the relay's seq exceeds the old fence. connectionSucceeded does not clear a SECURITY issue from the same generation.

Tombstone resurrection is real too. recoverableLocalDeletes only returns tombstones where tomb.actorId == the local actor. A returning stale device re-stamps X at its own counter+1, which is below the absent actor's tombstone. The wiped relay accepts it, while peers that hold the tombstone reject it via beatsCurrent (SyncReplayState.kt:124-134), and that includes snapshot application. Non-convergence between those peers and the relay/late joiners is permanent until X is edited again.

The lockout needs a room-wide Lamport counter above 10,000 plus 7 idle days. The false rollback warning and the divergence need only the wipe. Critical stands.

Android hard-wires `private val webSocketTransport = SyncWebSocketTransport()` (SyncManager.kt:254). The constructor (SyncManager.kt:159-164) takes only stores, a scope and a context. No unit test constructs SyncManager: grep finds it only in androidTest/TacMapChatLiveInteropTest.kt, which is opt-in and live. SyncManagerLiveSessionTest only exercises the pure acceptedV3Departure helper.

iOS owns `private var task: URLSessionWebSocketTask?` (SyncManager.swift:761) created via webSocketSession.webSocketTask (:1655). handleMessage (:2905), applyDeliveryNack (:3054) and applyHelloAckV3 (:3539) are all private. The SyncProtocolV3Tests that construct SyncManager test presence config, callsign bounds, room names and session-RNG failure; none feed frames.

CI runs only unit tests (android.yml:55-61 testDebugUnitTest/testReleaseUnitTest; ios.yml -only-testing:TacticalMapsTests).

The gap is real, and the defects in S6-01/03/07 sit exactly in these untested paths. It is a coverage gap, not a runtime defect, so I rate it medium rather than high; the behavioural consequences are filed separately.

The relay returns stale/retry:false whenever the incoming stamp is not newer than the stored one (index.ts:1190-1192, 1218-1227). The scratch test shows the loser receives [put, op-nack stale], and I re-ran it green. Both clients map stale to SECURITY and cancel the socket (Android SyncManager.kt:2051-2065; iOS SyncManager.swift:3072-3093).

The close path then does real damage:
- It clears chat transport with markPendingFailed=true, so the loser's in-flight chat messages are marked failed.
- It clears sessions and presence and reconnects with a full snapshot.

I tried to refute it with the ack-loss or reconnect re-send path, which would make it worse. The relay sameV3Record check needs the same sd, but after reconnect an own exact record in the snapshot gets baselined via resolvePendingModelApplication NONE → markModelBaseline (SyncManager.kt:2676-2697). So the only realistic trigger is a genuine same-object race.

There is no infinite loop: the winner's put was already applied live, so after reconnect the model matches the snapshot. The warning is transient; issueLifecycle clears it on the next clean generation. Even so, a false security banner, socket teardown, failed pending chat and a full-room re-download on an ordinary LWW loss is broken behaviour under a plausible condition (two editors on one object). High is fair, although frequency is limited to same-object races within about one RTT.

Android enterBackgroundPresenceOnly (SyncManager.kt:387-417) keeps the CONNECTED socket. detachMissionStateForKeyLock calls clearChatTransport, which sends nothing to the relay.

iOS updateLifecycle (SyncManager.swift:977-1007) calls clearChatSessionSecrets (:1551-1564). That only mutates local state and marks pending messages failed; it keeps the socket when backgroundPresenceEnabled && connected.

Both discard inbound frames before parsing (Android :1795-1797; iOS :1715-1727). No revoke or withdrawal frame exists in any of relay, Android or iOS (grep finds none).

The relay attachment still holds chatKey. routeChat (index.ts:1314-1336) routes both room frames and exact direct frames to that socket, and handleChat sends chat-ack. Peers keep the unit in chatRecipients: Android publishChatRecipients (:863-866) only filters on chatPeerKeys, iOS refreshChatRecipients only on activeSessions, and no leave is sent.

ADR-004 §1 (line 46-49) requires the key to be released on lock, and Verification item 5 (line 413) requires stale-key targets to produce a failure. Here the sender gets Routed for a message the recipient's code silently drops.

ADR-004 does say Routed is not proof of delivery. But this is a systematic false positive in the normal field posture (locked phone with background location), not a malicious-relay edge case. High stands.

broadcast() (index.ts:1556-1562) sends to every socket with no subscription filter. routeChat room scope also includes the background socket because its chatKey stays set (S6-04 root).

Peer foreground cadence is at most one loc per 5 s (UnitSyncPresenceCadence.foregroundInterval=5, SyncManager.swift:573; movement or fix-refresh driven, so stationary peers send less). The auditor's roughly 2 frames/s for 10 moving peers is an upper-bound but realistic estimate.

Android admits the frame to liveReceiveBudget before the backgroundPresenceOnly drop (SyncManager.kt:1779-1797). iOS does the same (SyncManager.swift:1703-1720). Status stays CONNECTED, so the LIVE 200-frame/10 s budget applies (SyncInboundFramePolicy.kt:101-105), and rejectInboundFrame closes with 1008 (:1829-1834).

After that close, Android calls backgroundTransportEnded (:1029-1030). The iOS handleDisconnect gate returns because foregroundReady is false (:1784-1787). Background presence therefore ends until the next foreground.

The constant inbound stream keeps the cellular radio out of idle for a mode whose whole purpose is a 1-60 minute egress cadence, which is major waste. The budget-trip half needs a burst (it overlaps S6-07), but the steady-state waste alone justifies high.

processWebSocketMessage calls touchActivity() for every non-ping frame (index.ts:805), including loc, chat and chat-key frames that need no storage. touchActivity does storage.put('meta:lastActivity') plus getAlarm (index.ts:1564-1568). These are relevant to the tests-plan dimension and are not covered, or only partly covered, by the findings.

1. **Delivery retries amplify bursts and can tear the socket down.**
   - Both clients re-send any op not acked within 1 s, then after 2, 4 and 8 s (Android SyncManager.kt:1165-1185; iOS SyncManager.swift:2221-2246).
   - Those re-sends count toward the relay's per-socket 200-message / 4 MiB window (index.ts:862-878) and its pending-queue caps (:741-751).

   - After 5 unacked attempts, both clients report SECURITY and cancel the socket (Android ~:1175-1181; iOS :2231-2238).
   - No test covers retry timing under latency.
   - Proving test: a scripted transport with 1.5 s ack delay and a 150-object publish. Assert no duplicate frames, and no 4008 or cancel.

2. **The room-wide pending admission closes innocent sockets.**
   - webSocketMessage closes whichever socket's frame arrives while roomPendingMessages ≥ 512 or roomPendingBytes > 8 MiB (index.ts:741-751).
   - When 3 or more clients burst at once (after a deploy, after a wipe, or during a bulk import), an idle peer's single loc or hello can get it closed with 4008.
   - Proving test: a vitest where 3 sockets each queue 180 puts while a 4th sends one loc. Today the 4th socket is closed.

3. **v3 tombstones are never garbage-collected.**
   - They count toward MAX_RECORDS=10,000 (index.ts:19; the only GC-style logic is v2 deletedAt at :906).

4. **The recoverableLocalDeletes resend at hello-ack is itself an unpaced burst.**
